title: Fermat 1637 margin claim
summary: Fermat annotates Diophantus: no positive solutions to a^n+b^n=c^n for n≥3; 'marvelous proof' too narrow for the margin. Open for 350+ years with only sparse special cases.

title: Two continents: elliptic curves vs modular forms
summary: Elliptic curves y^2=x^3+Ax+B produce fingerprints a_p by counting points mod primes. Modular forms (esp. weight 2) produce coefficient sequences a_p. Matching sequences are the modularity correspondence.
math: a_p = p+1-#E(F_p) (slogan); weight-2 modular form Fourier coefficients

title: Frey curve + Ribet level lowering
summary: Hypothetical FLT counterexample builds a Frey elliptic curve. Ribet (Serre's ε-conjecture) forces any modular twin into an extreme space: weight-2 forms of level 2. That space is zero-dimensional—no such form exists—so the curve cannot be modular.
math: Frey curve from (a,b,c,n); level lowering to N=2; dim S_2(Γ_0(2))=0

title: Wiles–Taylor: semistable modularity closes the trap
summary: Wiles (with Taylor) proves every semistable elliptic curve over Q is modular. Frey curves from FLT counterexamples are semistable, hence would be modular—contradiction. FLT follows. ~7 years attic work; modularity is the real target, FLT a corollary.
math: Semistable modularity ⇒ no Frey curve ⇒ no FLT counterexample

title: What the bridge is worth
summary: Modularity is an island of the Langlands dictionary. Full BCDT modularity and broader Langlands remain larger stories. Popular video compresses a multi-hour technical ladder.
